mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy shift, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by >0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a sharp economic slowdown, triggering a negative market reaction as corporate profits face dual pressures from reduced demand and supply chain disruptions, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., 60-day returns are positive in >40% of such instances).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% triggers a market reassessment of corporate profit margins under tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 6.0% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month reflects strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1.0% over a 3-month period signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, reducing corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls by >1.0pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and a drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic weakness, reducing consumer confidence and spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in >40% of such instances).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by GDP growth above 2.0% annualized), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,300,000 units signals a cooling in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, a decline in HOUST fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (i.e., 60-day returns are positive in >40% of such instances).
